extracted.intended_audience: ECCV 2026 reviewers (conference peer reviewers in computer vision)
extracted.subtask_description: Reviewer guidance for assessing ECCV 2026 submissions, covering core review principles, the new Contribution Types framework, review quality expectations, important policies, and conflict-of-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should look for what is good or stimulating in the paper and what knowledge advance it has made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage novel/brave concepts (novelty tolerance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to embrace novel, brave concepts, even if they have not been tested on many datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that a proposed method does not exceed state-of-the-art accuracy on an existing benchmark dataset is not grounds for rejection by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Types (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors assign one Contribution Type to their paper, which specifies how reviewers should assess it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since computer vision research encompasses a wide range of work, ECCV 2026 introduced Contribution Types to support fair, nuanced, and context-aware reviewing. Each type has its own evaluation criteria and weighting of factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: Theoretical foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'Theoretical foundations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an illustrative type; the guide notes that each Contribution Type (including theoretical work) will have its own evaluation criteria and weighting. Reviewers should assess theory according to appropriate standards for correctness, novelty, clarity of proofs/derivations, and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: New algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'New algorithms'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an illustrative Contribution Type, new algorithms should be judged according to their novelty, correctness, empirical behavior, clarity of presentation, and appropriate baselines — recognizing that weighting may differ from other types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: New datasets / benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'New datasets / benchmarks'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets/benchmarks are a distinct Contribution Type and should be evaluated on curation quality, scale, documentation, ethical considerations, representativeness, and provided evaluations; the guide emphasizes that such types have their own criteria and weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: New systems / applications
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'New systems / applications'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems/applications should be judged by system design, engineering contribution, utility, reproducibility, and evaluation appropriate to applied work; reviewers should apply the Contribution Type's specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: Empirical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'Empirical analyses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical analyses should be evaluated on experimental rigor, statistical validity, scope of experiments, reproducibility, and clarity of insights; weighting differs from other types per the Contribution Types framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: Position / opinion papers
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'Position / opinion papers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position/opinion submissions should be assessed for clarity of argument, originality of perspective, engagement with prior work, and potential to stimulate discussion; treat them under the Contribution Types-specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type: Survey / synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustrative Contribution Type listed is 'Survey / synthesis'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys and syntheses should be judged on coverage, organization, critical analysis, and value to the community; reviewers should apply the evaluation criteria appropriate to this Contribution Type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review specificity and detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be specific and detailed in their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion (more than scores) helps authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for recommendations, including specific feedback on ways authors can improve their papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of minor flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor flaws that can be easily corrected should not be a reason to reject a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between easily fixable issues and substantive problems that affect the paper's validity or contribution; encourage constructive suggestions for fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: No LLMs for reviews/meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) are NOT allowed to be used to write reviews or meta-reviews, whether run locally or via an API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict policy item defining forbidden review practices; reviewers must craft reviews themselves without LLM assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Strict deadlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the stated deadline for submitting reviews; late submissions may not be accepted or may affect the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are proprietary; do not share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must keep manuscript content confidential and must not disclose or distribute submission material outside the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (COI) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts include: same institution; recent collaborators (3 years); advisor-advisee; family members; recent close personal relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should declare these conflicts and avoid reviewing papers where such relationships exist; the listed categories define the primary COIs for ECCV 2026.
